text.p: Caspian Securities Inc reiterated its buy ratings on Brazil's telecoms giant Telebras and its Minas Gerais state unit Telemig after the release of new long-distance revenue sharing rates.

-- It also maintained market performer ratings on Telebras' Sao Paulo unit Telesp and Rio de Janeiro subsidiary Telerj after release of the rates used to figure how much they must pay to long-distance monopoly Embratel.

-- "The new Embratel revenue sharing agreement is more onerous for Telesp and Telerj than expected, while other local operators saw little change," Caspian analysts Joanne Showalter and Tony Figueiredo said in a report.
-- On average, the percentage of outbound long-distance revenues paid to Embratel by local Brazilian telephone companies rose to 27 percent in 1997 from 20.9 percent in 1996, they said.
-- But the average for Telesp, Telerj and Telemig, which account for 60 percent of Telebras' long-distance revenue, is much higher at 40.5 percent.
-- "This impies that the combined revenue payments to Embratel of the 27 (Telebras) subsidiaries is significantly higher than 27 percent," they added.
-- The rate rose to 45.6 percent from 29.5 percent for Telesp, jumped to 44.8 percent from 17.8 percent for Telerj and climbed to 31 percent from 24.6 percent last year, it said.
-- The firms are Telebras' three largest subsidiaries.

-- Telebras' preferred was up 0.4 percent at 149.30 reais, Telesp preferred rose 0.14 percent to 360.50 reais, Telemig common was off 1.26 percent at 157 reais and Telerj preferred jumped 2.39 percent to 173 reais at 1213 local/1513 GMT in Sao Paulo.
